attentionQuestions.question: The basic assumptions of the unit hydrograph theory are

options.text: Linear response and non-linear time invariance
linear response and linear time variance

attentionQuestions.explanation:
Unit hydrograph is based on following two basic assumptions:
(i) Time invariance: According to this assumption the direct run-off hydrograph for a given effective rain fall is always the same in catchment irrespective of the time when the rain fall or storm takes place.
(ii) Linear response: It is the single most important assumption in the theory of unit hydrograph. According to this assumption any variation in the input value is proportionally reflected in the outlet value.

attentionQuestions.question:
Consider the following statements pertaining to advantages of sprinkler irrigation:
1. Cropped area may be increased by 16%.
2. Upto 80% of applied water can be stored in the root zone of plants.
3. Heavy soil with poor intake cannot be irrigated efficiently.
4. It is not suited to crops requiring frequent and larger depths of irrigation, such as paddy.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
attentionQuestions.explanation:
Advantages of sprinkler irrigation:
• Land levelling is not required, and thus avoiding removal of the fertile soils as happens in other surface irrigation method.
• No cultivation area is lost for making ditches, as happens in surface irrigation methods.
Hence, it results in increasing about 16% of the cropped area.
• Fertilizer can be uniformly applied, because they are mixed with irrigation water itself.
• This method leaches down salts and prevents water logging or salinity.
• About 80% water application efficiency is possible i.e., upto 80% of water applied can be applied can be stored in root zone of plants.
• Labour cost is reduced as no land preparations are required.
• It can be used when there is scarcity in water because evaporation and percolation losses are less.
• It is especially adaptable to more humid regions.
Disadvantages of sprinkler irrigation:
• Under widely conditions and high temperatures, the water distribution and water application efficiencies are low.
• They are not suited to crops requiring frequency and larger depths of irrigation, such as paddy.
• Initially cost of the system is very high and the system requires a high technical skill.
• It requires large electrical power.
• Heavy soil with poor intake cannot be irrigated efficiently.

attentionQuestions.question: According to Khosla’s theory, the undermining of the floor starts from
attentionQuestions.explanation:
The undermining (piping) of the floor starts from the downstream end of the downstream pucca floor and if not checked, it travels upstream towards the weir wall. The undermining starts only when the exit gradient is unsafe for the subsoil on which the weir is founded. It is absolutely necessary to have reasonably deep vertical cut-off at the downstream and of downstream pucca floor to prevent undermining.

attentionQuestions.question: The Thiessen weights of 4 rain gauges A, B, C and D covering a river basin are 0.15, 0.25, 0.30 and 0.30 respectively. If the average depth of rainfall for the basin is 5 cm and rainfall recorded at B, C and D are 5 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm respectively, what is the rainfall at A?
attentionQuestions.explanation:
Average rainfall = ΣWeight × Rainfall
5 = 0.15 × P_A + 0.25× 5 + 0.3 × 4 + 0.3 × 5
P_A = 7 cm
